name: Rhode Island

events.title: Ratified the Constitution
events.text: Rhode Island ratified the Constitution on May 29, 1790, the 13th state to do so. The Constitution gave it 1 seat in the House until the first census.

events.title: 1790 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1790 census, Rhode Island's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats.

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 3rd through 27th Congresses (1793–1843), Rhode Island elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: 1800 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1800 census, Rhode Island kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: Advisory commission recommends maps
events.text: In 2011 the state created an 18-member advisory commission to recommend districts; the legislature could adopt, change, or ignore them. It passed a congressional plan in February 2012.

events.title: 2020 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2020 census, Rhode Island kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 2022 plan enacted
events.text: A new 18-member advisory commission was formed in 2021. The legislature passed the congressional plan on February 15, 2022, and the governor signed it the next day; no court challenge appears to have been filed.

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.
